THE WAVING GUIDE

Keep an eye
on the details.

A routine look from ground level can help you spot a flag that needs attention.

GET A QUOTE

Look for visible wear.

Note frayed edges, tears, faded colours, detached clips or a flag that no longer moves as expected. Describe what you can see without climbing or reaching into the operating system.

Match the replacement to the display.

Record the existing design, dimensions and attachment style if known. Keep approved brand artwork available for custom flags and note any differences between sites.

Plan around the property.

Replacement intervals vary with exposure, fabric, use and condition. An agreed inspection schedule can help a property team decide when replacement is appropriate.

Leave damaged systems alone.

Do not force a jammed rope or approach loose overhead components. Describe the issue and ask for an appropriate assessment.
